blocks.para: To create an OS-as-website.
I wanted to see how close I could get Windows 3.1 feeling ‘decently’ native on a modern mobile device, enabling someone to browse this OS across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
The rules for this included keeping as much of the work as possible within the guest (Windows) and with little-to-no HTML/CSS styling within the host (browser).
This is the result.
This was only possible with agents; I would not have the time, patience, or attention necessary to build this without it. Consider this a form of artwork.
• PVDISP.DRV: A custom display driver that connects with the emulated graphics card
• PVMOUSE.DRV: A mouse driver to provide absolute pointer positioning, enabling both tap and mouse movement
• PVMON.EXE: A “broker” that publishes window geometry, runs commands, and arranges the shell into a phone column.
• PVHOOK.DLL: A library to hook Windows’ window management, enabling us to park popups and dialogs in off-screen tiles so they never paint over their owner
• PVDPI.EXE: A tool to swap SYSTEM.INI/font set for the device’s pixel density at boot
• PVSYS.FON: a system font at 120dpi
• LCD.EXE: A tool to control the WebGL greyscale LCD effect from within the guest
• PHONE.EXE: Puts a phone-shaped frame on a desktop and makes the mouse behave like a finger
• ABOUT.EXE: this
• WINSOCK.DLL: A custom Winsock 1.1 to enable networking at 1MB/s+ through the host
• FETCH.EXE: a fetcher to test retrieval over our socket to the host
A fork of v86 that adds:

• Paravirtual display adapter: An emulated graphics card that tells Windows what shape the browser window is whenever it changes, plus the ability to copy a rectangle of pixels on command, so dragging a window or scrolling doesn’t crawl
• Paravirtual socket device: enable the host to provide DNS/TCP/TLS and keeps the TCP stack out of the guest

• Compositor: Cuts Windows’ screen into per-window layers and re-stacks them for mobile devices, while remaining disabled on desktop. Each window’s contents shrink to fit a phone while its title bar stays finger-sized.
• Touch: tap/drag/two-finger scroll/pinch, momentum, edge-swipe window cycling, long-press right-click
• Emulator in a worker: moves the emulator to a worker to avoid blocking the main browser thread
• LCD shader: simulate a late-1980s/early-1990s greyscale LCD panel with crosstalk bleed and backlight inconsistency
• Custom “boot” screen: displays while the OS snapshot loads
• Soft-keyboard accessory bar: enables Ctrl/Alt/Del/F-keys/arrows on mobile devices
• Screen-reader layer: describes the open windows to a screen reader, which otherwise sees nothing but a canvas
The path opens a program. /solitaire opens Solitaire, /notepad opens Notepad, /jezzball opens JezzBall, and so on. This note is /about.
